newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller says amnesty program "ill-advised".
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller says amnesty program "ill-advised".

text.p: The New York State Comptroller on Friday predicted the state's tax amnesty program would fail to meet its revenue target and said it was proving to be "ill-advised."
In his February cash report, H. Carl McCall added the state's cash balance is $106.8 million above what the Pataki Administration projected in January.
"This report appears consistent with a higher estimate of revenues, which the governor acknowledged at the end of February," he said in prepared remarks.

Separately, the state budget director, Patricia Woodworth she still looks for a $1.6 billion surplus in the 1997 fiscal year, which ends on March 31. "I am confident that the budget will remain on target and for the second year in a row New Yorkers will realize a budget surplus," she said, in prepared remarks. The fiscal 1996 surplus totaled about $455 million.
McCall noted that the amnesty program only took in $222 million through February, which was less than half the gross amount estimated for the year.

In order to meet its net target of $110 million, the state needs a gross total of $450 million. "It is clear that the amnesty program is turning out to be ill-advised and that we will not reach that target."

Through February, tax collections rose 3.7 percent from a year-ago to $32.1 billion. But due to the Pataki Administration's tax cuts, revenues from personal income tax withholding were down 2.2 percent, though estimated personal income taxes shot up 18.3 percent. As a result, total personal income tax revenues were 4.3 percent higher at $17.5 billion.

For the first 11 months of fiscal 1997, sales tax revenues rose 5.1 percent over a year-ago, and consumer taxes and fees gained 2.7 percent to $8.5 billion. Business taxes gained 3.6 percent to $5 billion, and other taxes firmed 1.5 percent to $1.1 billion. Miscellaneous receipts climbed 3.7 percent to $8.1 billion, mainly due to one-shots. Spending for all government funds fell slightly to $53.5 billion.
